extraction.body: Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private. These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator. The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android. Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use. These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android. Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up. “That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.” In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store. And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews. Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates. Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations. The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience. The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution.

Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices.
Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account.
Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly.
For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods.
It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases.
Google is also updating how users discover applications and games.
Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps.
The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves.
Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment.
This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code.
The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on.
If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves.
As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful.

extraction.body: Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store. The new feature from Google makes it easier for people to turn everyday needs into custom applications, even without traditional programming skills. Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices. Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account. Initially, the feature is rolling out to adults aged 18 and older in the United States and select markets. These apps will remain private, absent from public Play Store search results and accessible only to their creators. Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly. The update reflects a broader change in software development. As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful. They can be built for one person, one household or a specific problem that existing software does not adequately address. Until now, people experimenting with AI-generated Android applications faced a gap between creating an app and conveniently using it on their own devices. They could build web applications or work through more technical installation processes, but distributing a native Android app through Google Play traditionally required a developer account and additional publishing steps. Google’s new feature simplifies that process. Users can describe an idea to Gemini through Google AI Studio, refine the generated application and launch it for personal use. The potential applications are straightforward. Someone could create a specialised expense tracker that matches their budgeting habits, a personalised workout log or a household organiser tailored to their family. A student could build a revision tool around a particular subject, while a small business owner could experiment with a simple inventory application. These tools do not need to compete with established apps or attract thousands of downloads. Their value comes from solving a specific problem for the person who created them. This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code. It does not eliminate the need to test software or understand its limitations, but it lowers the technical barrier to experimentation. The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution. Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies. Users who want to distribute their creations publicly must move to a professional developer account and pass the platform’s standard trust and safety reviews. This creates a clearer path from experimentation to publication. A personal project can begin as a private tool, be shared with a small group and eventually become a public product if it proves useful. For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods. It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases. The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves. Google is effectively moving beyond the idea that every useful application must first become a conventional public product. However, the distinction between personal and public apps remains important. An app generated for individual use may contain bugs, mishandle information or produce unreliable results. Private distribution does not automatically make software secure or accurate. Users will still need to be cautious about the permissions they grant and the information they enter. Initially, the feature is rolling out to adults aged 18 and older in the United States and select markets.

They can be built for one person, one household or a specific problem that existing software does not adequately address.

sources.title: Google Play now lets you ‘vibe code’ and launch your own personal Android apps
passages: "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play.

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.
Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update.

According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required.

Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC.
Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog.
Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse.

However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release.
Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment.

extraction.body: Google is rolling out a massive wave of updates to the Google Play Store today, and the headline feature completely changes how everyday users can build and run software on their devices. According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required. Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update. "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play. Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account. No Developer Account Needed: You don't have to pay registration fees or jump through publishing hoops to get your custom app onto your phone. Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog. Future Sharing: Rolling out today in the U.S. (for users 18+), the feature is currently limited to your own device. However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release. Smarter discovery and Googlebook optimizations Alongside personal app creation, Google is overhauling how you find content across different form factors and inside the store itself: Built for Googlebook & Beyond: The Play Store is adapting better to non-phone screens. On the new Googlebook platform, apps optimized for large screens are now pushed front and center. Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse. Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment. Additionally, "Play in Gemini" is rolling out soon to bring app and game recommendations directly into your Gemini chats. Sports Topic Pages: You can now follow live scores and jump directly into streaming apps for major soccer leagues, including the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and MLS. "Gamer DNA," 48-hour Sprints, and PC expansions Mobile and PC gaming on Google Play also received a hefty set of community and discovery upgrades: Game Finder & Gamer DNA: Rolling out in the U.S. today, Game Finder analyzes how you play and your stated preferences (mechanics, art styles, genres) to build your "Gamer DNA." It uses this profile alongside data from similar players to recommend titles that actually match your taste, rather than just pushing what is popular. You can also curate and soon share custom "Game Playlists." Sprints & Sidekick: Available globally today, "Sprints" are fast-paced, 48-hour micro-challenges that match you with groups of two to five players. Community Posts: Game detail pages now feature a built-in Q&A forum with automatic language translation so players can help each other out directly in the store. Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC. Google is also expanding free limited-time Game Trials to PC titles. Finally, Google is adding a new Family Link feature that lets parents share a child's general age range directly with apps to ensure age-appropriate experiences without oversharing personal data. Most of these updates, alongside this week's Play Fest points event, are beginning their rollout today. Be sure to check your Play Store app over the next few days to see the new layout and tools in action.

coreStoryFacts.text: Are you tired of ad overload in free, single-task apps?
Or, can you not find an app that fits a weirdly specific need?
Now you can make custom apps for your own Android phone, even if you have zero coding experience.
One Tuesday, Google announced that anyone with a standard Google account can build personal apps in Google AI Studio.
These apps will run on your own device, launched from a private part of Google Play, and won’t be included in the public Play Store.
You’ll be able to share your apps with close family and friends in the coming months, but you don’t have to.
Custom Android apps make app development a much more personal and potentially user-friendly experience.

The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs.
That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.

story.title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android

facts.text: Are you tired of ad overload in free, single-task apps?
Or, can you not find an app that fits a weirdly specific need?
Now you can make custom apps for your own Android phone, even if you have zero coding experience.
One Tuesday, Google announced that anyone with a standard Google account can build personal apps in Google AI Studio.
These apps will run on your own device, launched from a private part of Google Play, and won’t be included in the public Play Store.
You’ll be able to share your apps with close family and friends in the coming months, but you don’t have to.
Custom Android apps make app development a much more personal and potentially user-friendly experience.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android
It just got a whole lot easier to vibe code the exact Android app you need - no developer experience required.
Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday.
A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs.
That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.”
In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends.
Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications.
Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations.
Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.
Google Play vibe-coded apps can now run privately on Android devices, allowing users to create personal software with artificial intelligence without publishing it to the public Play Store.
The change is significant, but it does not mean Google is abandoning its control over Android distribution.
Personal apps must still comply with Google Play’s existing policies.
Announced on Tuesday, October 13, the feature connects apps created through Google AI Studio with users’ Android devices.
Instead of opening a paid developer account and publishing an app for a public audience, users can launch their creations through a standard Google account.
Google plans to introduce secure sharing with selected friends and family in the coming months, giving users another option between keeping an app personal and releasing it publicly.
For Google, that pathway could encourage more people to build within its ecosystem rather than relying on alternative installation methods.
It also keeps Google Play relevant as AI makes software creation easier and competition over app distribution increases.
Google is also updating how users discover applications and games.
Its Game Finder feature uses personal gaming preferences to recommend titles, while Ask Play is gaining comparison tools to help users evaluate similar apps.
The strategic question is whether the Play Store can evolve from a marketplace for finished products into infrastructure for software that users create themselves.
Traditional app development generally requires developers to anticipate the needs of a broad audience and build products that can serve enough users to justify the investment.
This is the promise of vibe coding: people can describe what they want in natural language and allow AI to generate much of the underlying code.
The next stage will depend on whether users can move beyond novelty projects to build applications they genuinely rely on.
If that happens, the future of mobile software may be defined not only by the apps available to everyone, but also by the ones individuals can build for themselves.
As AI tools make coding more accessible, applications no longer need to be designed for millions of users to be useful.

"Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play.

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.
Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update.

According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required.

Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC.
Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog.
Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse.

However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release.
Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment.

Also: ‘What’s your AI stack?’ The new job interview question you need to answer You’ll be able to share your apps with close family and friends in the coming months, but you don’t have to. If you do share an app you create and it takes off, Google will provide a “pipeline to graduate into a professional developer account,” meaning you’ll be able to share your app globally via the Play Store. To get started, access the tool in Google AI Studio . There is an app creator in AI Studio, but that’s intended for professional developer accounts and requires USB debugging connected to a PC. This new tool works with that same creator, but it lets you install your app on a personal device with a single click and later directly share it instead of utilizing a public Play Store listing. In the tool, you describe what you want in a prompt, and AI does the rest. While the app is under creation, you’ll see options to add features you might have missed. You can make light edits once the app is complete, or you can completely scrap it and start again. There’s no charge to experiment and build an app. Custom Android apps make app development a much more personal and potentially user-friendly experience. It could be a fantastic option for replacing apps on your phone that you only use for a single thing – like a habit tracker, a calculator or converter, or a specific counter or timer. The ability to make an app with AI isn’t new, but the big selling point here is that you can make an app completely for yourself . Also: I used a free, open-source AI tool to build a working app – in two days My wife had surgery recently, and part of her recovery involves an array of specifically timed medicines, supplements, and liquids. She downloaded a simple tracker app to stay on top of things, but the app was loaded with ads to the point it was too frustrating to use. A monthly subscription was offered to nix the ads, but she didn’t want to pay for an app that would only be used for a few months. Searching for similar apps yielded similar results. With Google’s new system, it seems like it would be simple to make a custom app that avoids both the ads and the fees. And even better, you can tailor this app specifically to what you need. Perhaps the best part about this system is that an app you make doesn’t have to be commercially viable, and it doesn’t even have to be an app that anyone else needs. It just has to work for you . extraction.body: Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private. These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator. The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android. Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use. These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android. Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up. “That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.” In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store. And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews. Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates. Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations. The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience. sources.title: Google Play now lets you ‘vibe code’ and launch your own personal Android apps
passages: "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play.

Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account.
Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update.

According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required.

Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC.
Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog.
Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse.

However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release.
Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment.

extraction.body: Google is rolling out a massive wave of updates to the Google Play Store today, and the headline feature completely changes how everyday users can build and run software on their devices. According to a new announcement from Google, the Play Store is transitioning from a place where you simply download existing apps to a platform where you can launch the ones you create yourself with no developer background required. Here is a quick breakdown of everything arriving in the latest Google Play update. "Vibe code" and run personal apps without a developer account The biggest addition today is the ability to build custom Android apps using Google AI Studio and deploy them directly to your own device through Google Play. Google specifically highlights that users can now "vibe code" personal projects - like a custom stat-tracker for a local rec league or a hyper-specific family organizer - and launch them using just a standard Google account. No Developer Account Needed: You don't have to pay registration fees or jump through publishing hoops to get your custom app onto your phone. Private and Secure: These personal apps remain completely separate from the public Play Store catalog. Future Sharing: Rolling out today in the U.S. (for users 18+), the feature is currently limited to your own device. However, Google notes that in the coming months, you will be able to share your custom apps privately with a close circle of friends and family, or eventually graduate the project to a professional developer account for public release. Smarter discovery and Googlebook optimizations Alongside personal app creation, Google is overhauling how you find content across different form factors and inside the store itself: Built for Googlebook & Beyond: The Play Store is adapting better to non-phone screens. On the new Googlebook platform, apps optimized for large screens are now pushed front and center. Cars with Google built-in are getting an adapted UI, and Android XR users now get an immersive 3D space where apps surround them as they browse. Ask Play & Play in Gemini: "Ask Play" can now generate side-by-side comparisons between similar apps, breaking down key differences and user sentiment. Additionally, "Play in Gemini" is rolling out soon to bring app and game recommendations directly into your Gemini chats. Sports Topic Pages: You can now follow live scores and jump directly into streaming apps for major soccer leagues, including the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and MLS. "Gamer DNA," 48-hour Sprints, and PC expansions Mobile and PC gaming on Google Play also received a hefty set of community and discovery upgrades: Game Finder & Gamer DNA: Rolling out in the U.S. today, Game Finder analyzes how you play and your stated preferences (mechanics, art styles, genres) to build your "Gamer DNA." It uses this profile alongside data from similar players to recommend titles that actually match your taste, rather than just pushing what is popular. You can also curate and soon share custom "Game Playlists." Sprints & Sidekick: Available globally today, "Sprints" are fast-paced, 48-hour micro-challenges that match you with groups of two to five players. Community Posts: Game detail pages now feature a built-in Q&A forum with automatic language translation so players can help each other out directly in the store. Big Games & Trials: Major titles like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are arriving on Play (with REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill coming soon), complete with cross-save support between Android mobile and PC. Google is also expanding free limited-time Game Trials to PC titles. Finally, Google is adding a new Family Link feature that lets parents share a child's general age range directly with apps to ensure age-appropriate experiences without oversharing personal data. Most of these updates, alongside this week's Play Fest points event, are beginning their rollout today. Be sure to check your Play Store app over the next few days to see the new layout and tools in action.

The screen could be used to show information such as weather updates, calendar events and music controls. Apple is also reportedly developing a specialised operating system for the device focused on smart home controls. HomePod mini may be integrated with S11 chip Apple is also expected to introduce an updated HomePod mini. The overall design may remain largely unchanged, while an upgraded S11 chip could improve performance and Siri responsiveness. The speaker could also get tighter integration with Apple’s smart home ecosystem and potentially new colour options. New Apple TV could double down on performance The third expected launch is an updated Apple TV. The device is rumoured to receive a more powerful chip, potentially the A19 or A19 Pro, which could improve gaming, streaming and multitasking. However, the notice does not specify what particular content was considered illegal, nor does it detail the specific grounds cited by MeitY. Apple directed the developer to contact the ministry for further information. sources.title: Apple launches HomeView: Here’s what the $299 Siri AI smart home hub can do - The News International
passages: Apple has unveiled HomeView, a new AI-powered smart home hub featuring a seven-inch screen, facial recognition and upgraded Siri capabilities.
Apple said its upgraded Siri AI can answer questions and hold conversations that users can continue on their iPhones or iPads.

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home,” Apple's marketing chief Greg Joswiak said.
The launches mark Apple's second major product event under CEO John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook in September.
The device also supports FaceTime calls, music playback and smart home controls, allowing users to monitor security cameras, adjust thermostats and lock doors.
The company also announced a new Apple TV 4K priced at $299 and an updated HomePod Mini costing $149.
HomeView can be mounted on a wall or placed on a table and supports up to six household members
The device, announced on Tuesday, will cost $299 and become available on November 13, according to CNBC.

sources.title: Apple launches HomeView: Here’s what the $299 Siri AI smart home hub can do - The News International
passages: Apple has unveiled HomeView, a new AI-powered smart home hub featuring a seven-inch screen, facial recognition and upgraded Siri capabilities.
Apple said its upgraded Siri AI can answer questions and hold conversations that users can continue on their iPhones or iPads.

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home,” Apple's marketing chief Greg Joswiak said.
The launches mark Apple's second major product event under CEO John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook in September.
The device also supports FaceTime calls, music playback and smart home controls, allowing users to monitor security cameras, adjust thermostats and lock doors.
The company also announced a new Apple TV 4K priced at $299 and an updated HomePod Mini costing $149.
HomeView can be mounted on a wall or placed on a table and supports up to six household members
The device, announced on Tuesday, will cost $299 and become available on November 13, according to CNBC.

(NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications. The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. The Company is committed to building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of EAI Brain & Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions, and EAI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications.

The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. The Company also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform designed to connect robotic assets, service capabilities, customer demand, and ecosystem partners, further strengthening its robotics commercialization and service ecosystem.

(NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront. Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry. Faraday Future Announces FF EAI Robotics’ Employee Incentive Plan to Allocate Approximately 25% of Its Outstanding Shares for Stock Options for Its Core Team, Aiming to Establish an Industry-First Partnership Model

Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI.

“The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.”

FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms.

At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection.
Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders

FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy.

First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront.

Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry.

Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector.

Founded in 2014, Faraday Future (FF) is a U.S.-based Physical AI ecosystem company dedicated to reshaping the future of robotics and mobility solutions through AI innovation and technologies. FF focuses on two major product strategies within the Embodied AI (EAI) robotics business: EAI humanoid and bionic robots, and EAI automotive-focused robots. By building a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem comprising the EAI Brain and Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions and the EAI Data Factory, FF aims to create an evolutionary flywheel: scaled device delivery, data collection and training, continuous evolution of the EAI Brain, stronger product capabilities, and even larger-scale delivery and deployment. Through this flywheel, FF seeks to maximize its commercial value and advance the development of Physical AI.

FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. Upon completion of the acquisition, the Company will focus on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization, and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products, and industry solutions.

The Company is committed to building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of EAI Brain & Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions, and EAI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications.

The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. The Company also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform designed to connect robotic assets, service capabilities, customer demand, and ecosystem partners, further strengthening its robotics commercialization and service ecosystem.

Faraday Future Announces FF EAI Robotics’ Employee Incentive Plan to Allocate Approximately 25% of Its Outstanding Shares for Stock Options for Its Core Team, Aiming to Establish an Industry-First Partnership Model Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI. “The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.” FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms. At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection. Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy. First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront. Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry. Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector. Los Angeles, CA (September 23, 2026) – Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced a long-term employee equity incentive plan at its robotics subsidiary, FF EAI Robotics Inc. (“FFR”). FF EAI Robotics is allocating approximately 25% of the capitalization of FF EAI Robotics on a fully diluted basis as the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan to provide long-term equity incentives for the Company’s core management team, key leaders, and key employees. The proposed plan is intended to further strengthen FF’s robotics strategy and help FF EAI Robotics establish a partnership model in the robotics industry. Such equity of FFR is not convertible to equity of FFAI.

“The equity incentive plan is intended to create a long-term incentive and value-sharing mechanism,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. “By linking the core team’s long-term interests to the growth of our robotics business and enterprise value, we aim to align the interests of our team, the Company and our stockholders. We believe this will encourage a partnership mindset, sustained commitment and long-term value creation.”

FF aims to build the world’s only “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World. Its “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem is taking shape, and Robot World 2.0 is complete. Spanning three robot forms, five series, 11 models and 24 products, FF believes its lineup offers the most complete range of robot forms, broadest size coverage and most models of any U.S. robotics company—providing industries and users with an EAI Brain, solutions and data across those forms.

At its 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch, FF launched nine EAI Device configurations across two robot forms, three series and five models: FF All-New Futurist, FF Master Mini, FX Aegis Hyper, FX Aegis Mega and FX Aegis Classic Ultra-W. All nine are now available for sale and delivery. FF also launched four Industry Productivity Solutions for K-12 Education, Research, Security and Inspection.
Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan Designed to Maximize Value for FF Stockholders

FF believes the global robotics industry is at a pivotal stage in its transition from technology validation to large-scale commercial deployment. Against this backdrop, the long-term equity incentive plan is intended to help FF EAI Robotics attract, retain and motivate the talent needed to advance FF’s robotics strategy.

First, for FF stockholders, the plan is intended to maximize long-term stockholder value. By linking the core team’s incentives to the growth of the robotics business, FF aims to strengthen operating efficiency and value creation while keeping stockholder interests at the forefront.

Second, for the Company, the plan is expected to strengthen its ability to attract and retain top talent, encourage an entrepreneurial and partnership-oriented culture, and build the team needed to compete in the robotics industry.

Finally, for the industry, FF EAI Robotics aims to become the first robotics company to implement a partnership model, offering an example of how long-term talent incentives can strengthen organizational capabilities across the robotics sector.

FF focuses on two major product strategies within the Embodied AI (EAI) robotics business: EAI humanoid and bionic robots, and EAI automotive-focused robots. By building a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem comprising the EAI Brain and Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions and the EAI Data Factory, FF aims to create an evolutionary flywheel: scaled device delivery, data collection and training, continuous evolution of the EAI Brain, stronger product capabilities, and even larger-scale delivery and deployment. Through this flywheel, FF seeks to maximize its commercial value and advance the development of Physical AI.

passages: It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen.
HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more.
The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad.
A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.
The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device.
Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface.
To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information.
If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.

It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen. HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more. The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad. The centerpiece of the HomeView is a 7-inch square Liquid Retina display. To me, it looks like an enlarged Apple Watch, and the tabletop version with a base comes in Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink and Space Gray colors. This model has a base that contains a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators to bolster the audio performance of the two full-range drivers in the display. Connecting the screen and base together is a stainless steel hinge that allows you to adjust the viewing angle. If you prefer a wall-mounted option, Apple offers the HomeView without a base, but the overall functionality is the same. Interestingly, there are no buttons on the HomeView; the touchscreen display and your voice are the two ways to interact with the device. The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device. That second number is particularly important in the home, for early mornings or if you plan to place the HomeView on your nightstand. The smart display's main, passive screens are called Faces, which are customizable with things like art, photos and various clock designs. Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface. At the top of the display, there's a 12-megapixel FaceTime camera with Center Stage for video calls. Like the Echo Show and other smart displays, HomeView is certainly equipped for catching up with friends and family in a way you can see them. Additionally, the device supports voice and video apps, on top of native iOS apps like Calendar and Weather. HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access. And like Apple's HomePod speakers , you can handoff things like audio or even recipes from your iPhone by holding your handset close to the HomeView. Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari. So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView. And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that. To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information. The speaker also uses facial and voice recognition to distinguish between users, displaying a personalized interface and list of apps based on who is standing in front of the device. If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen. HomeView will also require you to periodically unlock your iPhone or iPad in order to use it, which you'll probably be doing constantly throughout the day anyway. There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning. A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric. The former worked with Apple on indoor and outdoor cameras along with a video doorbell, door lock and thermostat. The Schneider Electric collaboration is an additional option for a thermostat. Apple hasn't said when its Home Collection will be available, but it has released pricing on all of the devices, which range from $199-$349. These devices will also be easily discoverable by your iPhone, where you'll see a card like you would for setting up AirPods when you bring your phone near them. And as you might expect, you can control them all on HomeView and get live video feeds on the smart display. Both versions of the HomeView can be pre-ordered today with general availability scheduled for November 13.

passages: The HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker that aims to be a central access point for up to six members of a family to access and control Apple’s ecosystem of devices, apps, and the Siri generative AI chatbot that’s currently in beta.
You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door.
With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”

Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks. HomeView can also show a livestream for up to nine video feeds simultaneously.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door. With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets. Users can connect their HomeView profile to their Apple Intelligence-supporting iPhone or iPad and use the hub to access their Messages, Calendar, Reminders, and FaceTime.

“With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person—taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context,” Apple’s announcement says.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”

Apple’s first smart display uses a Liquid Retina (LCD) screen that Apple says has a brightness range of 0.3 to 500 nits. You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.

“The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer,” Apple’s announcement said.
The screen connects to the speaker base and tilts using a stainless steel hinge. The speaker base holds the device’s USB-C charging port.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made. Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today. It launches on November 13 for $299.

coreStoryFacts.text: It seems like an eternity since the first reports that Apple was working on a smart display to rival Amazon's Echo Show came out, and at long last the company has finally revealed its take on the smart home screen.
HomeView is a touchscreen device that acts as a hub for various connected devices, as well as a personalized control center for audio and more.
The device was built for Siri AI and can adapt its content and features based on which of your family members are using it by pulling data from their iPhone or iPad.
A big part of Apple's smart home push is the Apple Home Collection of devices designed with LG and Schneider Electric.
The display has a maximum brightness of 500 nits and goes all the way down to 0.3 nits, which is the lowest brightness Apple has ever offered on any device.
Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface.
To power Siri AI, the HomeView has an A18 chip, which also provides the level of data security required for an in-home device that will use so much personal information.
If you walk away from the HomeView, someone who tries to see what you were looking at will get a lock screen.
There's a special setting for overnight lulls here, so you won't have to unlock your phone before you start interacting with the HomeView in the morning.
Speaking of recipes, Apple developed a new recipe mode for Safari.
So long as you're looking at a recipe that meets Google's formatting standards, you'll get an easy to follow format on HomeView.
And if you need extra ingredients or to set a timer, Siri AI can help with that.
HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access.

The HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker that aims to be a central access point for up to six members of a family to access and control Apple’s ecosystem of devices, apps, and the Siri generative AI chatbot that’s currently in beta.
You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door.
With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.

That second number is particularly important in the home, for early mornings or if you plan to place the HomeView on your nightstand. The smart display's main, passive screens are called Faces, which are customizable with things like art, photos and various clock designs. Once the HomeView is unlocked, you'll see a Home screen with four areas for widgets, similar to how you can customize your Apple Watch interface. At the top of the display, there's a 12-megapixel FaceTime camera with Center Stage for video calls. Like the Echo Show and other smart displays, HomeView is certainly equipped for catching up with friends and family in a way you can see them. Additionally, the device supports voice and video apps, on top of native iOS apps like Calendar and Weather. HomeView functions like CarPlay in that you don't download apps to it, but the display will show your recently used apps on its menu for easy access. And as you might expect, you can control them all on HomeView and get live video feeds on the smart display. Both versions of the HomeView can be pre-ordered today with general availability scheduled for November 13.

sources.title: Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299
passages: The HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker that aims to be a central access point for up to six members of a family to access and control Apple’s ecosystem of devices, apps, and the Siri generative AI chatbot that’s currently in beta.
You can also set the screen to automatically adjust its brightness level based on how bright the room is.
Apple started taking preorders for HomeView today.

“With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door.
With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it,” Apple’s announcement said.

Mounting the HomeView to a wall requires a specific model that only comes in two (instead of four) colors, space gray and silver, and paying extra (starting at $60) for the wall mounts, which Schneider Home made.
Apple says that it created “two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically” for wall-mounted HomeViews.

“With Siri AI built into HomeView, users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery,” Apple said.
Apple is also marketing the HomeView as a way to leverage Siri AI, including asking it about “virtually any topic.”
Users can speak to HomeView to control smart home devices, such as, for example, telling Siri to close the smart blinds or activate smart locks.

Competing with devices like the Amazon Echo Show , HomeView uses its integrated camera to identify who’s using it and show them their profile, which users can personalize with their preferred apps and widgets.
Apple said that Siri requests can run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, where “data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.”
